items.figure:
NOT gate diagram:
A ───|>o─── Y

The small circle at the output indicates inversion.
steps: A NOT gate, also called an inverter, produces the complement of its input.
When the input is 0, the output is 1; when the input is 1, the output is 0.
Boolean expression: Y = NOT A (or Y = A̅).
Truth table:
A | Y
items.finalAnswer: A NOT gate reverses its input: Y = A̅.

Here, + denotes the OR operation.
steps: A truth table shows the output of a Boolean expression for every possible combination of its input values.
First, identify the input variables and the number of input combinations. For n inputs, there are 2ⁿ combinations.
List all possible input combinations, using 0 and 1 for each input.
Evaluate the Boolean expression for each combination and enter the result in the output column.
Example: Construct the truth table for Y = A + B, where + denotes OR.
The inputs A and B have 2² = 4 possible combinations.
Truth table:
A | B | Y = A + B
items.finalAnswer: A truth table lists every input combination and the output obtained by evaluating the Boolean expression.

items.figure:
Half-adder circuit:

A ──┬── XOR ── S
    │
B ──┴── AND ── C

Full-adder circuit using two XOR gates, two AND gates and one OR gate:

A ─────┐
       ├── XOR ── X ──┐
B ─────┘               ├── XOR ── S
Cin ───────────────────┘

A ─────┐
       ├── AND ── P ──┐
B ─────┘               │
                       ├── OR ── Cout
X ─────┐               │
       ├── AND ── Q ──┘
Cin ───┘
steps: A half-adder adds two one-bit binary numbers. It has two inputs, A and B, and two outputs, Sum (S) and Carry (C).
Half-adder Boolean expressions: S = A XOR B; C = A AND B.
Half-adder truth table:
A | B | S | C
A full-adder adds three one-bit inputs: A, B and the carry input (Cin). It has two outputs, Sum (S) and Carry output (Cout).
Full-adder Boolean expressions: S = A XOR B XOR Cin; Cout = (A AND B) OR (A AND Cin) OR (B AND Cin).
Full-adder truth table:
A | B | Cin | S | Cout
A half-adder has no carry input, so it is used to add two bits when there is no incoming carry.
A full-adder has a carry input, so it can add two bits together with the carry from the previous stage.
items.finalAnswer: A half-adder adds two bits; a full-adder adds two bits and an incoming carry.

steps: To add two 4-bit binary numbers, connect one half-adder and three full-adders in series. The carry output of each stage becomes the carry input of the next stage.
Let the two numbers be A3A2A1A0 and B3B2B1B0, where A0 and B0 are the least significant bits.
Stage 1: Connect A0 and B0 to a half-adder. S0 = A0 XOR B0; C1 = A0 AND B0.
Stages 2–4: Connect A1, B1, C1 to the first full-adder; A2, B2, C2 to the second full-adder; and A3, B3, C3 to the third full-adder.
For each full-adder stage i (i = 1, 2, 3): Si = Ai XOR Bi XOR Ci; Ci+1 = (Ai AND Bi) OR (Ai AND Ci) OR (Bi AND Ci).
The outputs are S3S2S1S0, with C4 as the final carry. Thus, the complete sum is C4S3S2S1S0.
Half-adder truth table (used for the least significant bit):
A | B | S | C
Full-adder truth table (used for the other three bits):
A | B | Cin | S | Cout
Half-adder Boolean expressions: S = A XOR B; C = A AND B.
Full-adder Boolean expressions: S = A XOR B XOR Cin; Cout = (A AND B) OR (A AND Cin) OR (B AND Cin).
items.finalAnswer: A 4-bit adder uses one half-adder for the least significant bits and three cascaded full-adders for the remaining bits.
